caption:
A drone deal with Trump's sons' firm. A five-year missile gap. 25,000 deportees. Abroad, news. Here, five weeks of nothing.

The Financial Times broke the Powerus deal September 16, Bloomberg the missile warning September 18, and the Forbidden Stories consortium the deportation figures September 21; each ran at three or more major foreign outlets. Reuters carried the first and The Washington Post, a consortium partner, the third. In checks from October 12 to 26, none of the other major US outlets we could check followed on any of them; ABC couldn't be checked.

Save this. Check back in a week.

Counts as reported abroad at 3+ major foreign outlets; counts as missing at home when none of the 11 major US outlets ran it, not counting whoever broke it. Board: news.schmim.com

deep.timeline_lede: From India to Rawalpindi in eleven weeks.

timeline.e: An Indian defence firm says Powerus gave it an exclusive licence to build its Guardian interceptor drone in India.
Powerus executives meet Field Marshal Asim Munir at army headquarters in Rawalpindi. A US embassy official attends.
Powerus announces an order from Pakistan's defence ministry and a framework deal with its army. No value or contents given.
Filings show a fund of Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump set to own about 9.9% of Powerus after a merger.
The merger closes. Powerus trades on Nasdaq as PUSA.

deep.timeline_note: As of Oct 31: no public word on what Pakistan ordered, what it cost, or any US approval.

claims.say: The contracts were won on merit; Trump's sons had “no involvement on the business side.”
He is a passive investor with no role in the company's management or operations.
There are no conflicts of interest.
The talks covered procurement, production and capacity building. It did not mention the deal.

deep.unknown: What was ordered and its value. Whether US export approval was sought; Powerus says the deal is subject to it. Eric Trump's spokesperson could not be reached.
